judgment.reasoning_summary: The problem requires finding the smallest n such that any set of n distinct positive integers contains two elements whose sum is divisible by 7. This is a classic application of the pigeonhole principle. We need to consider the possible remainders when dividing by 7, which are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. If we have 7 or more distinct positive integers, by the pigeonhole principle, at least two of them must have the same remainder when divided by 7. If these two numbers have remainders r and 7-r (e.g., 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4), their sum will be divisible by 7. Therefore, the smallest n is 7.
